newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares mixed at open, OTC stocks lead.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares mixed at open, OTC stocks lead.

text.p: Singapore shares were mixed at the open on Tuesday with investors' focus on speculative Malaysian over-the-counter stocks.

"There is light profit taking in Singapore stocks but the focus is still on OTC stocks. There was a wave of profit taking for OTC stocks early in the morning but they are bouncing back now," said a broker with a local firm.

Malaysian issues hogged the top actives list with the exception of some new Singapore issues like Chuan Soon Huat and Second Chance. The UOB OTC index was up 0.96 points to 1,287.61 after about an hour of trading.
The Straits Times Industrial index was up 2.14 points to 2,227.49. Total market volume was 94 million with 117 gainers against 92 losers.

Trading based Lindeteves-Jacoberg led the gainers list to hit a new high of S$2.04 before easing to S$1.99, up 11 cents, in moderate dealings. A dealer said there was no fresh news on the company but noted that fund managers like the stock.

Foreign tranches of local banks were early losers with DBS, UOB, OCBC and OUB all easier by between 10 to 40 Singapore cents each in moderate dealings. Singapore Press foreign led the losers with a 70 cent drop to S$26.60. -- Doreen Siow 65-8703092
